title: Afghan Veteran Nabi and South African Skipper Tahir Power Amazon Warriors to CPL Opening Win
excerpt: Guyana Amazon Warriors bowled out Jamaica Kingsmen for 117 and chased the target in 14.1 overs, with Shai Hope's unbeaten 56 sealing a comfortable six-wicket victory at Sabina Park.
body:
• Guyana Amazon Warriors defeated Jamaica Kingsmen by 6 wickets in the CPL 2026 opener at Sabina Park, Kingston, on August 13
  • Afghanistan's Mohammad Nabi contributed 19 off 15 balls with the bat in the chase, adding to his all-round value for the defending champions
  • West Indian Shai Hope anchored the chase with an unbeaten 56 off 41 balls (2 fours, 4 sixes), while Glenn Phillips blasted 28 off 17 at the top
  • South African-origin captain Imran Tahir, 47, continues to lead the franchise after steering them to back-to-back Global Super League titles

The Guyana Amazon Warriors began their CPL 2026 campaign with a clinical six-wicket demolition of the Jamaica Kingsmen at Sabina Park on August 13, chasing down 118 in just 14.1 overs after bowling the hosts out for 117.

It was a statement of intent from the defending champions, who won the toss and chose to bowl — a decision vindicated by a disciplined bowling display that kept Jamaica under pressure throughout their innings.

Bowling First, Bowling Well

The Warriors' bowling attack, captained by the evergreen Imran Tahir, strangled the Kingsmen batting lineup from the start. Jamaica's top order found no rhythm against a varied attack that mixed pace with spin.

South Africa-born Reeza Hendricks and captain Rovman Powell — two of Jamaica's most experienced batters — could not build the partnerships needed on a pitch offering pace and bounce. Even Andre Russell, one of T20 cricket's most destructive hitters, was kept in check.

The Kingsmen were bowled out for 117 in 19.4 overs, a total that never looked competitive at a ground where 160-plus is typically par in T20 cricket.

The Diaspora Connection

The CPL has long been a melting pot of international cricket talent, and the Warriors' squad this year is particularly notable for its diaspora representation. Mohammad Nabi, the 41-year-old Afghan all-rounder, is among the most well-traveled cricketers in franchise leagues worldwide. Born in Logar Province, Afghanistan, Nabi grew up during the Soviet-Afghan War and learned his cricket in refugee camps in Pakistan before becoming Afghanistan's first IPL player in 2017.

At 47, South African-born captain Imran Tahir remains one of the most effective leg-spinners in T20 cricket. Born in Lahore, Pakistan, Tahir represented South Africa in international cricket before becoming a franchise cricket mainstay. His leadership was instrumental in the Warriors winning back-to-back Global Super League titles earlier this summer.

"We are perfectly set up. The boys know what is expected. We just go out there and do the business."

— Imran Tahir, Captain, Guyana Amazon Warriors

South African-born Dwaine Pretorius adds further depth to the squad's multinational character, while Guyanese local Shimron Hetmyer provides Caribbean flair.

Hope Anchors the Chase

New Zealand's Glenn Phillips gave the Warriors a flying start, smashing 28 off 17 balls with 4 fours and a six before falling to Andre Russell. The innings lost early momentum when Mavendra Dindya was dismissed for a duck and Hetmyer fell for 1, both to Russell, leaving the Warriors at 29 for 3.

Nabi steadied things with a composed 19 off 15 balls before being caught off Vitel Lawes. But it was West Indian keeper-batter Shai Hope who took charge, playing the definitive innings of the match. Hope's unbeaten 56 off 41 balls — including 2 fours and 4 sixes — was measured and clinical, pacing the chase perfectly.

Quentin Sampson hit the winning runs, finishing unbeaten on 13 off 9 balls as the Warriors cruised home with 35 balls to spare.

What's Next

The Warriors will look to build on this opening win as they chase a CPL title to add to their consecutive GSL crowns. For Jamaica Kingsmen, the challenge is clear: their bowling lacked the firepower to defend a modest total, and the batting failed to produce a score worth defending.

The CPL 2026 season runs through September, with the final scheduled at Providence Stadium in Guyana — familiar territory for the Warriors and their vocal home support.
